To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the multiple molecular forms of hexokinases found in human red blood cells are not isozymes but rather are the same protein with different isoelectric points.

the human erythrocyte hexokinase (HEXK) isoenzymes are not only different in their isoelectric points (pI), but are also different in their kinetic properties, in their sensitivity to heat, and in their age dependence.
the human red blood cell contains multiple molecular forms of hexokinases, and that the relative proportions of the different forms are age-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of hexokinase in red blood cells.
the characterization of the multiple forms of human red cell hexokinase which have been separated by chromatography on DEAE cellulose.

the characterization of multiple forms of human red cell hexokinase, which are present in different proportions in red blood cells of different age, and the elucidation of their possible functional role.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of different hexokinase isoenzymes in human erythrocytes is a function of age of the cells and that the predominant form is the one which is characteristic of the fetal erythroblast.

the presence of hexokinase I, II, and III isozymes, as reported in other tissues, is not the rule for red blood cells, and that the multiple forms of hexokinas found in red blood cells are probably not the result of the action of a proteolytic enzyme, since the isozymes are stable to proteolytic enzymes, and since the pattern of isozymes is not altered when the red cells are stored at 4 degrees C.
the three major forms of human red cell hexokinase, which differ in their isoelectric point, are all catalytically identical, but are present in different amounts in the red cells of different age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the red blood cell hexo kinase system is a complex one which is not only age and species dependent but also dependent on the type of tissue from which the red cells were derived.
the multiple forms of hexo- kinase present in red cells are the result of the expression of different genes, each one coding for a specific isozyme.
human red blood cells possess three forms of hexokinases which are separable on ion exchange chromatography, are different in their isoelectric point, but are otherwise identical.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of different hexokinase isoenzymes may be related to the different metabolic requirements of the red blood cells in the fetus, newborn, and adult.
the presence of hexokinase in multiple forms in red blood cells is not a peculiarity of the rabbit erythrocyte.
the presence of more than one form of hexokinase in human erythrocytes is not an artifact of the preparation procedure, but rather is an intrinsic property of the enzyme.
